title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-26 10:00 PST | Duration 45m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Finova - Lead ML Eng), Luis Ramirez (Finova - Platform Eng), Anika Singh (Finova - Security), Tom Becker (Finova - Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — we'll run through last week's benchmark updates, network routing issues, and the upgrade window for the private control plane. I think Ethan has the numbers.
[00:18] Ethan: yeah, hi. um, so on the bench — we ran the resnet-ish, sorry, the LLM throughput tests against the 8xA10 pool in the VPC, and saw a steady 12% perf improvement after enabling the newer kernel set. Note: KV cache warm up still adds variance.
[00:41] Sara: got it. 12% is great. Is that from the batching changes or the kernel swap?
[00:48] Ethan: mostly kernel selection plus a small tweak to the continuous batching param. we bumped max_batch_latency from 20ms to 15ms for the latency-sensitive routes. that reduced tail latency but increased cost a hair.
[01:12] Luis: on cost — can you quantify the "hair"? we need to put numbers in the pilot report for finance.
[01:20] Ethan: roughly 6% more GPU time per token for the low-latency config; but when you enable prefix caching it offsets ~4% on our sample workloads. so net is about 2% higher for very latency-sensitive traffic.
[01:38] Anika: quick security note — we need to confirm KMS integration works with our internal HSM. last week the key exchange failed on the staging cluster.
[01:49] Maya: yes, that's high priority. Ethan, can you walk through the error logs we saw?
[01:56] Ethan: sure. The agent log shows an auth error — it was a misconfigured IAM role mapping on the customer-side cross-account role. the Redwood side retried as expected but the initial handshake failed. looks like Tom updated the role yesterday?
[02:12] Tom: yeah, I pushed an interim change, turned out the trust policy didn't include the management role for the private-control-plane. reverted that and then the KMS handshake succeeded.
[02:24] Anika: ok — is there an audit entry? we need to show proof for compliance.
[02:29] Ethan: yes, we have audit logs; I'll export and share a filtered view.
[02:35] Maya: perfect. Next, network routing — Sara, you had intermittent 502s when traffic crossed AZ boundaries?
[02:44] Sara: right — on Tuesday we saw a spike of error rates when the smart routing fell back from the preferred region to the secondary. seemed like the health checks timed out.
[02:55] Ethan: that was during a burst; the retry policy sent some traffic to the older model variant which lives on a different AZ. the model variant mapping is fine, but the VPC route table had some stale entries for the nat-gw replacement.
[03:12] Luis: hmm we had an infra change Friday night — replaced NAT gateways for cost reasons. I guess the route table wasn't propagated to the private-control-plane instances.
[03:21] Maya: this is why we wanted the orchestrated routing check in the pilot. We can add a preflight that validates route propagation before cutover.
[03:31] Tom: we can run the preflight. should we run it in the staging cluster first?
[03:36] Ethan: yes, run staging preflight, then a canary in non-prod, then prod. also note — the preflight needs to validate both control-plane egress and customer-subnet egress for KMS calls.
[03:51] Sara: on the upgrade window: are we still targeting next Tuesday evening?
[03:55] Maya: tentative yes, Tues 11/2.. sorry I mean 12/2? oops — we need to confirm date. (laughs) Let's confirm — we suggested Dec 2nd 22:00 UTC in the doc.
[04:08] Luis: Dec 2nd at 22:00 UTC works for our team. We'll schedule a maintenance window and notify SRE.
[04:15] Anika: only ask is that we get a runbook and rollback steps. we can't be in the dark if KMS fails mid-upgrade.
[04:22] Ethan: absolutely — the runbook will include rollback to previous control-plane image, route table restore, and an immediate KMS key switch back. we'll also include an automated verification that token encryption/decryption works post-upgrade.
[04:36] Maya: great. Benchmarks — sara, any user-facing perf regressions?
[04:42] Sara: not really. the subjective latency improved for our chat flows, but we saw a 3% increase in tail CPU on our frontend proxies when under sustained load. Could be client-side backpressure interacting with the shorter batch latency.
[05:00] Ethan: yes, that matches the profile — smaller batches increases more frequent kernel invocations, which can raise load on proxy layers. we can tune the client-side retry/backoff to smooth spikes.
[05:11] Tom: do we have a recommended proxy config for nginx/gateway?
[05:15] Ethan: we'll share our recommended nginx timeouts and upstream keepalive params — will include in the ops doc.
[05:22] Maya: Security checklist — Anika, besides KMS/HSM, anything else?
[05:27] Anika: SAML SSO test still needs to be run against our staging IdP; we had a user mapping mismatch last week. also need confirmation of RBAC roles in the Redwood Console for Auditor role.
[05:39] Maya: ok, we'll add SAML test steps and confirm Auditor role perms. Ethan, can you confirm auditor-read-only covers audit logs and model metadata?
[05:49] Ethan: yes, auditor role includes read-only access to audit logs and model catalog metadata; it does not allow rollouts.
[05:56] Luis: FYI procurement asked about data residency — we need confirmation that no tokens are persisted outside our VPC.
[06:03] Maya: Redwood Private keeps inference compute inside the customer's VPC; control plane metadata may be in the private control plane depending on the deployment. We'll need to call out what metadata is stored.
[06:12] Ethan: I'll prepare a short doc mapping metadata categories (logs, telemetry, model artifacts) to storage locations.
[06:18] Sara: that would help — procurement also wants a short SLA for pilot uptime targets, even if informal.
[06:24] Maya: propose 99.5% for the pilot, we can formalize later.
[06:29] Tom: that seems reasonable.
[06:33] Maya: quick catch-up on the demo app — any regressions?
[06:36] Sara: no major regressions. small prompt parsing differences after kernel swap but we can tune generation params.
[06:44] Ethan: note: function-calling had a small mismatch with our tool schema because one of the LLM outputs had punctuation differences; likely transcription/tokenization. not a showstopper.
[06:56] Anika: also to note: please ensure TLS mutual auth is enabled for the private-control-plane endpoints. we saw a cert chain mismatch on Friday but it's resolved.
[07:06] Maya: thanks. Ok let's recap next steps and action items.
[07:12] Sara: quick Q — any impact on canary traffic routing if we enable the new kernel globally?
[07:18] Ethan: we can gate kernel selection by model variant and route. so canary traffic can stay on old kernel until we flip it.
[07:25] Luis: perfect.
[07:28] Maya: all right — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the security packet and the benchmark CSV.
[07:34] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional imperfect auto-transcription (e.g., \"V P C\" instead of \"VPC\", \"K V cache\" for KV cache). Speakers sometimes overlap; timestamps are approximate.
summary: Weekly POC sync: performance improved (~12%) after kernel and batching tweaks; small cost increase (~2% net) for latency-sensitive config. KMS/HSM handshake initially failed due to IAM/trust policy but was resolved; audit logs available. Intermittent 502s traced to stale route table after NAT gateway replacement; preflight validation proposed. Upgrade window proposed for 2025-12-02 22:00 UTC (to be confirmed) with runbook and rollback. Action items: share security package, run SAML test, export audit logs, provide benchmark CSV and nginx proxy recommendations.

Ethan to export filtered audit logs and benchmark CSV
Tom/Luis to schedule staging preflight and maintenance window for Dec 2nd 22:00 UTC
Ethan to publish nginx/gateway recommended timeouts and keepalive settings
Anika to run SAML SSO test against staging IdP and report mapping issues
